chapter.li: LEChapter6 Verse1 After finishing his speech to the people, king Benjamin decided to make a record of the names of everyone who had made a covenant with God to keep His commandments. VerseEnd Verse2 It turned out that everyone except the little children had made this covenant and had taken upon himself or herself the name of Christ. VerseEnd Verse3 After king Benjamin had completed all his duties and consecrated his son Mosiah as the new ruler and king over his people, he transferred all the kingdom’s responsibilities to him. Additionally, he appointed priests to teach the people, so that they could hear, learn, and understand God’s commandments, and to remind them of the covenant they made. Finally, he dismissed the crowd, and everyone returned home with their families. VerseEnd

Verse4 Mosiah took his father’s place as king at the age of 30, which was approximately 476 years since Lehi and his family left Jerusalem. VerseEnd Verse5 King Benjamin lived for three more years after his son took the throne, and then passed away. VerseEnd Verse6 King Mosiah was a righteous ruler who followed the Lord’s ways, obeyed His commandments, and kept His judgments and statutes. VerseEnd

Verse7 He encouraged his people to cultivate the land, and he himself worked hard on the crops to set a good example and not be a burden on his people. He followed his father’s example. As a result, there were no conflicts among his people for three years. VerseEnd
